Text-verified 11/11 (2026-09-28, tu-ov002-batch-0928). The earlier Behavior near-miss (0xcf8 against 0xcfc) was not a register-allocation limit: under '#pragma defer_codegen off' mwccarm generates a function at the next top-level token after its closing brace, not at the brace, so the '#pragma opt_strength_reduction off' written directly after Behavior was still in force when Behavior was generated. Compiled alone with defer_codegen off, Behavior matches; with a trailing opt_strength_reduction off and nothing between, it does not; with any top-level declaration between, it does. The TU now places InitResources' own extern block between the two, and all eleven members match with emission order exact.

The loose source hand-called fBase_c::operator new(sizeof(dMap_c)), fBase_c's base constructor, and stored _ZTV7dBase_c then _ZTV6dMap_c. dMap_c and dBase_c declare no constructor, so the implicit default constructor emits exactly that sequence and the factory is `return new dMap_c();`, which binds fBase_c's inline operator new. The TU keeps `#pragma defer_codegen off`, so the factory is written last, after GetPosOnMinimap.
